self_improvement.title: Self-improvement
self_improvement.subtitle: While you are away, the assistant tries small changes to how it works. It keeps a change only when a measurement on tasks from your own work shows that it helps.

error.unavailable: Self-improvement is not running in this app. Restart Dodaios. If this message stays, the app log says why.
error.load: The measurements could not be loaded ({detail}). Check that Dodaios is running, then try again.

state.running_first: No round has run yet. The first one starts when you have been away for {minutes} minutes.
state.running_body: The last round was {when}. The next one comes after {next}, once you have been away for {minutes} minutes.
state.running_due: The last round was {when}. The next one comes the next time you are away for {minutes} minutes.
state.stopped_body: Nothing is tried, measured or changed until you resume. What it already learned stays in effect.
state.readonly_body: A newer version of the app wrote these records. This version only shows them and changes nothing.

empty.title: Nothing is measured yet
empty.body: To measure itself, the assistant first builds test tasks from your own memory and messages while you are away. When there are enough, it checks itself on them, and this page shows whether it got better, what it changed and what proved each change.

recall.name: Memory
recall.about: Does the right memory come up for a message, and nothing when none is needed?

first_move.name: First move
first_move.about: Does the assistant reach for the right tool first, and say in one line what it takes on before it does?
first_move.building: {n} test tasks from your own chats with the assistant so far. Measuring starts when there are enough to decide on: {need} in the part it decides on, which holds {have} now.
first_move.no_tasks: There are no tasks from your chats for this area yet. They come from answers you let stand, and from answers the assistant got right after you corrected it.

brief.name: Briefs
brief.about: Does the brief the assistant writes for a coding agent point at the files the work turned out to need?
brief.building: {n} test tasks from your past coding work so far. Measuring starts when there are enough to decide on: {need} in the part it decides on, which holds {have} now.
brief.no_tasks: There are no tasks from your past coding work for this area yet. They come from requests you typed into a coding agent and the pull request that was merged for them.
brief.range_unclear_cheaper: As far as measured it is as good as shipped: the quality difference lies between {low} and {high} points, and that includes zero. Its message and brief are {pct} shorter.

area.meaning: How many more of 100 test tasks the assistant solves as it is now than as it was shipped.
area.range_better: The true difference lies between {low} and {high} points, so the gain is certain.
area.range_worse: The true difference lies between {low} and {high} points: as it is now, it does worse than as shipped.
area.range_unclear: The difference is not certain yet: the true value lies between {low} and {high} points, and that includes zero.
area.scores: now {now}, as shipped {shipped}, on {n} tasks it never learned from
area.waiting: {n} tasks from your work are ready. The first measurement comes with the next round.
area.no_tasks: There are no tasks from your work for this area yet, so nothing is measured here.
area.range_unclear_cheaper: As far as measured it is as good as shipped: the quality difference lies between {low} and {high} points, and that includes zero. Its prompt is {pct} shorter.
area.building: {n} test tasks from your own memory and messages so far. Measuring starts when there are enough to decide on: {need} in the part it decides on, which holds {have} now.

curve.title: Advantage, round by round
curve.caption: Points, with the range the true value lies in
curve.few: The curve appears after the second round that measures this area.

stack.title: What I changed in myself
stack.none: Nothing yet. Every value is as it was shipped.
stack.kinds: Three kinds of change: values it tuned and proved on tasks, how it steers coding agents, proved on half of your requests, and notes it wrote for itself, which are in effect but not measured yet.
stack.note_title: A note it wrote for itself
stack.note_gone: This note is gone from the memory.

effect.unclear: no clear difference on {n} tasks (between {low} and {high})

detail.not_checked: Not checked again yet. The next round does that.
detail.admitted_on: Measured on {n} tasks set aside for deciding, {when}.
detail.checked_on: Measured on {n} tasks that no change was decided on, {when}.
detail.note_unmeasured: Not measured yet: nothing can tell yet whether this note helps. It is in effect until you take it back.

author.tuner: The tuner, which tries nearby values on practice tasks
author.memory-learner: The assistant, after a tool failed and a later call worked
author.rsi-selector: The steering learner, which tries one change at a time on half of your coding requests
author.lines: The line learner, which tries your messages without one of their standing lines on practice tasks

nights.title: The last rounds
nights.updated: The app was updated from {from} to {to}. Everything learned was checked again.
nights.idle: Looked, and found nothing to measure yet.
nights.built_one: Built 1 test task from your own memory and messages.
nights.built_other: Built {count} test tasks from your own memory and messages.
nights.erased_one: Erased 1 task about a memory that is gone.
nights.erased_other: Erased {count} tasks about memories that are gone.
nights.stored_one: Stored 1 task from your past coding work.
nights.stored_other: Stored {count} tasks from your past coding work.
nights.deferred: No model could be asked, so no tasks were built.
nights.spent: Model calls: {calls}, about {share} % of a usage window.
nights.spent_unread: Model calls: {calls}, within the fixed limits (the plan's usage could not be read).

candidates.title: Waiting to be measured
candidates.row: proposed {when}, waits until there are enough new tasks to decide

resting.title: Resting after an update
resting.restale: Still in effect. The shipped value it was learned against changed with an update, so it is measured again first.
resting.dormant: Rests without effect, because this version cannot use it. It applies again as soon as a version can.

how.title: How it works
how.practise_body: It tries other values on one part of the tasks.
how.decide_body: A change goes in only when it proves itself on tasks it never practised on.
how.check_body: Later rounds check each change again on other tasks and take back what no longer helps.
how.limits: A learning round runs when you have been away from the computer for {minutes} minutes, at most once in {hours} hours, at any time of day. It also runs while the app's window is closed, as long as "Keep agents running after closing" is on in Settings.
how.models: Building test tasks asks a model only while the measurements still lack tasks: until there are enough to decide on, or nothing new is left to build them from.
how.measure_first_move: Measuring the first move and the briefs replays your earlier requests on the assistant's own plan, until the round's comparisons are done.
how.privacy: The memories and messages used for this go only to the provider the assistant already answers on. Memories marked sensitive are never sent.
how.budget: Every call runs on the assistant's own subscription or a local model, never on a key that is billed per token. No call starts while a usage window of your plan is {full} % full, and one round uses at most {share} % of a window.
how.fallback: When the plan's usage cannot be read, for example with a local model, fixed limits apply instead: {calls} calls a round to build tasks ({ramp} in the first rounds) and {replays} replays. No round ever makes more than {ceiling} calls of one kind.
how.last_round: Model calls in the last round: {calls}, about {share} % of a usage window.
how.last_round_unread: Model calls in the last round: {calls}. The plan's usage could not be read, so the fixed limits applied.

recall_entity_boost.title: Weight of names in a memory
recall_entity_boost.about: How much a memory moves up when it names a person or thing from the message.

recall_pinned_boost.title: Weight of pinned memories
recall_pinned_boost.about: How much a pinned memory moves up in a search.

recall_recency_floor.title: Weight of old memories
recall_recency_floor.about: How much weight a very old memory keeps. At 1, age does not matter.

recall_recency_days.title: How fast memories age
recall_recency_days.about: Over how many days the freshness of a memory fades.

recall_fetch_factor.title: Breadth of a memory search
recall_fetch_factor.about: How many candidates a search ranks, as a multiple of the number it returns.

recall_turn_limit.title: Memories per message
recall_turn_limit.about: The most memories one message may bring up.

recall_turn_max_chars.title: Room for memories per message
recall_turn_max_chars.about: The most characters the memories for one message may take in the prompt.

recall_relative_floor.title: Closeness to the best hit
recall_relative_floor.about: How close to the best hit a memory must score to be shown.

recall_min_score.title: Minimum match for a memory
recall_min_score.about: How well a memory must match before it is shown at all. At 0, any match is shown.

recall_lesson_base.title: Starting rank of a lesson
recall_lesson_base.about: Where a fitting lesson ranks against the best search hit, before its own fit counts.

recall_lesson_cap.title: Highest rank of a lesson
recall_lesson_cap.about: How far above the best search hit a lesson may rank at most.

lessons_recall_threshold.title: Fit needed for a lesson
lessons_recall_threshold.about: How many of a lesson's words a message must share for the lesson to come up.

lessons_recall_limit.title: Lessons per message
lessons_recall_limit.about: The most lessons one message may bring up.

lead_first_line.title: Opening line before a tool
lead_first_line.about: Beside each of your messages: write one short line that takes the task on before using a tool.

lead_brief_line.title: Wording of the brief line
lead_brief_line.about: Beside each of your messages: how the assistant is asked to look up the files before it briefs a coding agent.

daily.title: In daily use
daily.summary: {pct} of your {n} requests in the last {weeks} weeks went through without a correction, a repeat or a stop.
daily.caveat: This shows what happened, not what caused it: the requests of one week are not those of the next. The measured areas above compare like with like.

policy.hold: Waits for the checks and asks for fixes
policy.fewer_fixes_one: Asks for at most one fix
policy.shorter_wait: Waits at most {minutes} minutes for the checks
policy.brief_line: Adds a line to the first brief
policy.other: Changes how coding agents are steered
policy.on_trial: on trial on half of your requests since {when}
policy.claim_pass: kept only if clearly more requests pass
policy.claim_cost: kept only if it costs less and nothing gets worse
policy.claim_p: kept only if fewer fixes are needed and nothing gets worse
policy.proof_pass: Passed {with} of {n} requests, against {without} of {m} without it (at least {low} points)
policy.proof_cost: {diff} less per request in cost and time, on {n} requests against {m} without it (at least {low} less)
policy.proof_p: {diff} fewer fixes per request, on {n} requests against {m} without it (at least {low} fewer)
policy.measured_on: Measured on {n} of your requests with it and {m} without it, {when}.
policy.about: How Dodaios hands coding work to agents for this kind of work, this model and this coding tool: whether its answer waits for the checks, how many fixes it asks for, and what the first brief says. It was tried on half of your requests and compared with the other half.
policy.probation: On probation: the first run under it that weakens a check takes it back by itself.

lead_first_line.off: Dropped the line beside your messages that asks for a short opening line before the first tool.
lead_first_line.on: Put back the line beside your messages that asks for a short opening line before the first tool.

lead_brief_line.v0: Put back the shipped wording of the line beside your messages that says how to brief a coding agent.
lead_brief_line.v1: The line beside your messages now asks in fewer words to look up the files before briefing a coding agent.
lead_brief_line.v2: The line beside your messages no longer asks to look up the files before briefing a coding agent.
